goal: Give msfslogger's React/Vite client (client/src/**), which today has zero automated coverage, a component/page-level test framework (Vitest + React Testing Library, matching the backend's existing Vitest convention) and a Playwright browser-integration suite that exercises real user journeys — authentication, core data visualization/interaction, error handling and loading states — against a real scratch server and scratch SQLite database, never the user's live server on port 3000 or live flights.db. Wire both suites into .github/workflows/ci.yml so they run on every push/PR, produce a visible test report, and a regression in a covered journey blocks merge.
frozen_decisions: Never touch the user's live dev server (port 3000) or live flights.db, in CI or locally.
npm run build / vite build must never be run directly against this checkout for verification — only against a scratch copy of the tree.
Node 20 via nvm for every command.
Playwright's target in CI is a fresh scratch server + scratch/seeded SQLite DB on its own port, started and torn down by the CI job itself.
Playwright + Vitest/RTL (to match the existing backend Vitest convention) is the expected default absence of a strong reason otherwise.
Out of scope: replacing/reducing backend unit tests; visual regression/perceptual testing.
A task that needs a small server-side seed/reset hook for deterministic e2e fixtures is a backend task; framework setup + specs is frontend.
DevOps handles .github/workflows/ci.yml wiring — plan that as a DevOps-owned task at the end, gated on the implementation tasks being approved.
Journeys to cover: Authentication flow; core data visualization and interaction flows; error handling and loading states.
requireSameOrigin means Playwright must hit a same-origin scratch server (not a Vite dev server on a different port proxying to the API).
This run adds to the existing CI pipeline (.github/workflows/ci.yml), not a new one.
sequencing_rationale: Design must freeze the directory/tooling layout, the Playwright test-user auth mechanism, the seed/reset script's contract, the scratch server+DB provisioning recipe and the CI job shape before any implementer writes a file — every later task's file names, npm-script names and acceptance-criteria commands depend on names this decides, so Design is phase 1, reviewed on its own before Implement starts.

Phase 2 splits along the domain seam the intake already drew: the seed/reset CLI is backend (src/**, composes existing db/auth functions, no new schema or endpoint) and the Vitest/RTL + Playwright scaffolding is frontend (client/**). The two share no files and neither depends on the other's output, only on the frozen design, so they run in parallel.

Phase 3's journey specs depend on phase 2 being reviewed and proven working: Playwright needs a real scratch server it can log into (from the frontend scaffolding's global-setup) seeded with real fixture rows (from the backend seed script); RTL needs the Vitest/RTL config. Auth is split from the data-visualization + error/loading specs because it touches a disjoint page (Login) and needs no seeded fixture data, while error/loading states are natural companions to the data pages they appear on — this keeps all three phase-3 tasks' allowed_paths disjoint so they can run in parallel under one role (frontend_sr).

RTL component-level tests (T-008) are kept separate from the Playwright browser-level specs (T-006/T-007) on purpose: they assert the same loading/error states in isolation with a mocked fetch, fast and deterministic, complementing rather than duplicating the slower real-browser journeys — the same inspector-plus-suite split the backend already uses (ENVIRONMENT.md's Verification section).

CI wiring is deliberately last and DevOps-owned: the escape hatch (a human running these suites by hand against a scratch server, proven in phases 2-3) ships before the automation that runs them unattended on every push. It only makes sense once the exact build/seed/start/run/teardown commands are proven to work.

Every phase ends in a reviewer task, and phase N+1's first task depends on it, so a drifted or mis-scoped implementation is caught before later tasks — some of which touch files phase-2 tasks also touched (root/client package.json) — ever run concurrently with it.

phases.name: Design the test contract
phases.ships: The contract every later task depends on — test directory/tooling layout, how Playwright authenticates without real credentials, how the seed script and scratch server/DB are provisioned, and the CI job shape — is frozen and reviewed, so implementation tasks can proceed without hitting an undecided question mid-task.

phases.name: Seed script and test-framework scaffolding
phases.ships: A scratch server can be built, seeded with deterministic fixture data via a CLI, and started on its own port; a Vitest/RTL component test runs; a Playwright spec logs in for real against that scratch server and passes — the whole pipeline proven end to end before journey coverage is written.

phases.name: Journey coverage
phases.ships: Authentication, core data visualization/interaction, and error/loading-state journeys each have passing automated tests — browser-level (Playwright) and, for the states that benefit from it, component-level (RTL) — runnable on demand against a scratch server.

phases.name: CI wiring
phases.ships: Every push and PR runs the full frontend unit and Playwright suites automatically, publishes a visible test report, and a failure in any covered journey blocks merge.

tasks.title: Freeze the frontend test-framework, Playwright auth/seeding, scratch-provisioning and CI contract
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-17-frontend-integration-tests/design.md with five numbered sections (so downstream tasks can cite exact slices) deciding everything the intake flagged as open: where frontend component tests and Playwright specs live and how they're invoked; how Playwright authenticates as a test user without real credentials; the backend seed/reset script's contract; the scratch server+DB provisioning recipe for local runs and CI; and the CI job shape.
acceptance_criteria: SS1 Directory & tooling layout: names the exact config files/directories for (a) Vitest+RTL component tests under client/src (config file, jsdom setup file, the client npm script that runs them) and (b) Playwright under client/e2e (config, spec directory, support/helpers directory, global-setup file, the client npm script that runs them); states how each is wired into existing npm scripts without touching the backend's own vitest config or tsconfig.test.json.

SS2 Test-user identity & Playwright authentication: names the literal test username/password (or env vars) both the backend seed script and Playwright must agree on; specifies that Playwright's globalSetup performs one real POST /api/auth/login against the scratch server and persists storageState (reused via playwright.config.ts's `use.storageState`) — a real login through the app's own auth routes, not a session forge or a requireAuth bypass.

SS3 Backend seed/reset script contract: names its file path (src/testSeed.ts), its CLI invocation, and that FLIGHTS_DB_PATH is mandatory with no default that could resolve to the live flights.db; lists the exact fixture rows it inserts — the operator user from SS2, and named flights/trips/planned legs (specific airports, dates, routes) sufficient for Home, AllFlights, FlightDetail and TripDetail to render deterministic non-empty content; states whether re-running it is idempotent or one-shot-only.

SS4 Scratch server & DB provisioning recipe: gives the exact env vars and values (PORT, FLIGHTS_DB_PATH, BIND_HOST, and the TLS choice — either TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE or ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_HTTP=1 with a loopback BIND_HOST, with a stated reason consistent with src/config.ts's actual startup guard) to build the client, seed a scratch DB via SS3, start the scratch server, and tear it down — usable identically by a human running Playwright locally and by the CI job in SS5; states this always runs against a scratch copy of the tree, never a developer's live checkout.

SS5 CI job shape & reporting: states which job(s) in .github/workflows/ci.yml run the new suites (added to the existing file, not a new workflow), the exact steps (Playwright browser install, client unit-test step, build+seed+start+run+teardown for e2e), which reporter(s) produce a report visible in the Actions run (e.g. Playwright HTML/JUnit uploaded via actions/upload-artifact), and confirms a failing test fails the job.
Contains no implementation code beyond short config/file-content sketches; every decision is stated as a rule, not left as 'TBD' or 'either works'.

tasks.title: Review the frozen test contract for completeness and consistency

acceptance_criteria: Each of design.md's five sections (SS1-SS5) is checked against T-001's acceptance criteria line by line; the verdict names any missing or ambiguous item by section.
Confirms SS2's Playwright auth mechanism is a real POST to /api/auth/login, not a session-cookie forge or a requireAuth bypass — bypassing it would leave the auth journey itself untested.
Confirms SS3's seed script cannot silently target the live flights.db: FLIGHTS_DB_PATH (or equivalent) is mandatory with no default resolving to process.cwd()/flights.db.
Confirms SS4's TLS/plaintext choice is consistent with src/config.ts's actual startup guard (would not fail config.ts's own validation).
Confirms SS5 adds to .github/workflows/ci.yml rather than introducing a second workflow file.
Verdict approve or request_changes, with concrete section:point findings, written to reviews/phase1-design.md.

The fixture rows inserted (flights/trips/planned legs) match design SS3's list exactly — same airports/dates/counts — verified by querying the seeded scratch DB and diffing against the design doc's list.
npx tsc (server build) compiles src/testSeed.ts with no type errors, run against a scratch copy of the tree per .claude/ENVIRONMENT.md, never this checkout.

tasks.title: Playwright journey: authentication flow
tasks.goal: Cover login success, login failure (wrong password), logout, session persistence across reload, and redirect-to-login when unauthenticated, against the real scratch server.
